--- title: "3.2 Scaling and Identification" --- - We cannot estimate the variance of the errors directly in categorical outcome models so we assume part of their distribution. Two ways to think about it: - [Latent variable derivation]{.underline}: *y\** is unobserved so we do not know how well we predicted in that metric - [Probability model]{.underline}: our predictions are in a different metric than the observed outcomes ![](images/binary-outcome-example.png){width=60% fig-alt="Predicted probabilities from a binary model, a declining curved line, plotted with the observed outcomes, which sit only at 0 and 1."} ## Identifying assumptions - All regression models are designed to produce the best fitting line; estimates are chosen so that the mean of the errors is 0 - In all regression models: $$y_{i} = F(\mathbf{x}_{i}\boldsymbol{\beta}) + e_{i}$$ - I.e., The outcome *y* is a product of some predictable function of the **x** variables (explained variation), and due to some unexplained variation $e_{i}$ - In a linear model, we can calculate $e_{i}$ directly as predictions and outcome are in same metric - In binary logit/probit, have to assume/set the error distribution - This effectively changes the scale of *y\** ### Assuming the error distribution - The probability model shown in the [prior section](3-1-binary-model-derivations.qmd#probability-model-generalized-linear-model) is a **binary logistic (logit) model**, with an assumption that the error variance is $\frac{\pi^{2}}{3}$ (SD ≈ 1.81)---made so that calculating predicted probabilities is easy $$Logit: \Pr(y_{i} = 1\,|\,\mathbf{x}_{i}) = \Lambda(\mathbf{x}_{i}\widehat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}) = \frac{\exp(\mathbf{x}_{i}\widehat{\boldsymbol{\beta}})}{1 + \exp(\mathbf{x}_{i}\widehat{\boldsymbol{\beta}})}$$ - A near identical model, the **binary probit model**, can be derived by assuming normally distributed errors (variance and SD = 1) - But calculating probabilities is much harder and requires calculus $$Probit: \Pr(y_{i} = 1\,|\,\mathbf{x}_{i}) = \Phi(\mathbf{x}_{i}\widehat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}) = \int_{-\infty}^{\mathbf{x}_{i}\widehat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\exp\left(-\frac{t^{2}}{2}\right)dt$$ ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## Stata ```{.stata-run} . twoway function phi = normalden(x), range(-5 5) || /// > function psi = exp(x) / (1 + exp(x))^2, range(-5 5) || /// > , ytitle("probability(observing given value)") xtitle("{it:y*}") /// > xlab(-4(2)4) title("[3.2.b] Standardized normal vs logistic PDF") /// > legend(order(1 "Normal PDF" 2 "Logistic PDF")) ``` ![](fig/cda-03_02_b-PDFs_CDFs.png){width=80% fig-alt="The standard normal PDF, taller and narrower, and the logistic PDF, shorter and wider, both centered at 0."} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(haven) # import Stata data and labels library(dplyr) # data manipulation library(ggplot2) # graphs library(modelsummary) # tables of results library(cleanplots) # graph scheme cleanplots_defaults() ggplot() + stat_function(fun = dnorm, aes(color = "Normal PDF"), xlim = c(-5, 5)) + stat_function(fun = dlogis, aes(color = "Logistic PDF"), xlim = c(-5, 5)) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-4, 4, 2)) + scale_color_discrete(limits = c("Normal PDF", "Logistic PDF")) + labs(title = "[3.2.b] Standardized normal vs logistic PDF", x = "y*", y = "probability(observing given value)", color = NULL) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](3-2-scaling-identification_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-1-1.png){fig-alt='The standard normal PDF, taller and narrower, and the logistic PDF, shorter and wider, both centered at 0.' width=80%} ::: ::: ::: Effectively, logit's *y\** will have a larger range than probit's ![](images/ystar-ranges.png){width=60% fig-alt="Two double-headed arrows: a shorter one labeled probit y-star and a longer one labeled logit y-star."} ### Graphical illustration of identification assumption - The size of the *β*'s cannot be interpreted directly since their magnitude reflects both: - The relationship between the *x*'s and *y*\* - ***Arbitrary*** identifying assumptions :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ![](images/identification-probit.png){fig-alt="Latent y-star regressed on x with a shallower line and narrower error distributions at several values of x."} ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ![](images/identification-logit.png){fig-alt="The same relationship with a steeper line and wider error distributions: the y-star scale is stretched."} ::: :::: - Effectively, logit and probit models are on different scales, with logit assuming a *y\** with a wider range ## Comparing logit and probit ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## Stata ```{.stata-run} . use "https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/cda_anes", clear (American National Election Study 2020 - Pre-election | CDA | 2021-09-26) . . drop if missing(age, hhincome, woman, lgb, race4, /// > edyrs, relimport, wrongtrack) (948 observations deleted) . . qui logit vote_trump hhincome edyrs i.woman i.lgb i.race4 /// > i.relimport i.wrongtrack c.age##c.age . est store logitmod . . qui probit vote_trump hhincome edyrs i.woman i.lgb i.race4 /// > i.relimport i.wrongtrack c.age##c.age . est store probitmod . . * Compare coefficients . esttab logitmod probitmod, nobase label mtitles("Logit" "Probit") /// > b(3) z(3) title("[3.2.h] Comparing coef estimates from logit and probit") [3.2.h] Comparing coef estimates from logit and probit ---------------------------------------------------- (1) (2) Logit Probit ---------------------------------------------------- Voting for Trump Household income (~) -0.000 -0.000 (-0.897) (-1.085) Education in years -0.140*** -0.078*** (-9.539) (-9.444) Woman -0.355*** -0.197*** (-5.289) (-5.170) LGB -1.164*** -0.623*** (-6.607) (-6.798) Black -2.928*** -1.531*** (-15.543) (-17.253) Hispanic -1.185*** -0.642*** (-9.382) (-9.285) Other -0.648*** -0.348*** (-5.419) (-5.225) 2. Not important a~l -1.949*** -1.091*** (-18.279) (-18.475) Wrong track -3.308*** -1.897*** (-33.781) (-37.652) Age of R 0.027* 0.015* (2.129) (2.096) Age of R # Age of R -0.000* -0.000* (-2.509) (-2.399) Constant 5.268*** 2.952*** (13.692) (13.854) ---------------------------------------------------- Observations 6857 6857 ---------------------------------------------------- z statistics in parentheses * p<0.05, ** p<0.01, *** p<0.001 ``` ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} anes <- read_dta("https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/cda_anes.dta") # Drop any missing data on the model IVs anes <- anes[complete.cases(anes[c("age", "hhincome", "woman", "lgb", "race4", "edyrs", "relimport", "wrongtrack")]), ] # Treat binary/nominal variables as factors using their value labels anes <- anes |> mutate(woman = as_factor(woman), lgb = as_factor(lgb), race4 = as_factor(race4), relimport = as_factor(relimport), wrongtrack = as_factor(wrongtrack)) |> droplevels() logitmod <- glm(vote_trump ~ hhincome + edyrs + woman + lgb + race4 + relimport + wrongtrack + age + I(age^2), family = binomial(link = "logit"), data = anes) probitmod <- glm(vote_trump ~ hhincome + edyrs + woman + lgb + race4 + relimport + wrongtrack + age + I(age^2), family = binomial(link = "probit"), data = anes) # Compare coefficients modelsummary(list("Logit" = logitmod, "Probit" = probitmod), statistic = "({statistic})", fmt = 3, stars = c("*" = .05, "**" = .01, "***" = .001), gof_map = "nobs", title = "[3.2.h] Comparing coef estimates from logit and probit") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: ### Correlation and ratio of logit/probit coefficients :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="45%"} | **Correlation(logit, probit)** | | |:------|------:| | betas | 0.9995 | | *z*-stat on beta | 0.9980 | ::: ::: {.column width="10%"} ::: ::: {.column width="45%"} | **Ratio(logit / probit)** | | |:------|------:| | betas | 1.7819 | | *z*-stat on beta | 0.9816 | ::: :::: - β's differ by a factor of about 1.8 - Sound familiar? $\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{3}} \approx 1.81$ - *z* statistics (in parentheses [above](#comparing-logit-and-probit)) are roughly equal ## Comparing logit and probit distributions - Predicted probabilities, Pr(*y* =1), are a function of the cumulative density function The **PDF** is in colors; the **CDF** is in black ![](images/pdf-cdf-bars.png){width=70% fig-alt="Bar chart of a discrete distribution from -4 to 4: colored bars for the PDF peak at 0, and black bars for the CDF rise from near 0 at -4 to 1 at 4."} ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## Stata ```{.stata-run} . twoway function phi = normalden(x), range(-5 5) || /// > function psi_std = (c(pi)/sqrt(3))*exp(c(pi)*x/sqrt(3)) / /// > (1 + exp(c(pi)*x/sqrt(3)))^2, range(-5 5) lpat(dash) || /// > , ytitle("probability(observing given value)") xtitle("{it:y*}") /// > xlab(-4(2)4) title("[3.2.c] Standardized normal vs standardized logistic P > DF") /// > legend(order(1 "Normal PDF" 2 "Standardized logistic PDF")) ``` ![](fig/cda-03_02_c-PDFs_CDFs.png){width=80% fig-alt="The standard normal PDF and the standardized logistic PDF almost overlap; the logistic is slightly taller at the center."} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Standardized logistic: logistic with variance 1 ggplot() + stat_function(fun = dnorm, aes(color = "Normal PDF"), xlim = c(-5, 5)) + stat_function(fun = dlogis, args = list(scale = sqrt(3) / pi), aes(color = "Standardized logistic PDF"), xlim = c(-5, 5), linetype = "dashed") + scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-4, 4, 2)) + labs(title = "[3.2.c] Standardized normal vs standardized logistic PDF", x = "y*", y = "probability(observing given value)", color = NULL) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](3-2-scaling-identification_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){fig-alt='The standard normal PDF and the standardized logistic PDF almost overlap; the logistic is slightly taller at the center.' width=80%} ::: ::: ::: \*For comparability, I've standardized the logistic distribution, to see how they differ ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## Stata ```{.stata-run} . twoway function Probit = normal(x), range(-3 3) || /// > function StdLogit = logistic(1.701*x), range(-3 3) lpat(dash) || /// > , title("[3.2.d] Standardized normal vs standardized logistic CDF") /// > xlab(-3(1)3) legend(order(1 "Probit CDF" 2 "Standardized Logit CDF") pos(6 > ) row(1)) ``` ![](fig/cda-03_02_d-PDFs_CDFs.png){width=80% fig-alt="The probit CDF and the standardized logit CDF from -3 to 3: the two S-shaped curves are all but identical."} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot() + stat_function(fun = pnorm, aes(color = "Probit CDF"), xlim = c(-3, 3)) + stat_function(fun = function(x) plogis(1.701 * x), aes(color = "Standardized Logit CDF"), xlim = c(-3, 3), linetype = "dashed") + scale_x_continuous(breaks = -3:3) + labs(title = "[3.2.d] Standardized normal vs standardized logistic CDF", x = "x", y = NULL, color = NULL) + theme(legend.position = "bottom") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](3-2-scaling-identification_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){fig-alt='The probit CDF and the standardized logit CDF from -3 to 3: the two S-shaped curves are all but identical.' width=80%} ::: ::: ::: \*In the CDFs, the two distributions are all but identical, so predicted probabilities from logit and probit are all but identical ## Comparing predicted probabilities ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## Stata ```{.stata-run} . est restore logitmod (results logitmod are active now) . predict prlogit (option pr assumed; Pr(vote_trump)) . lab var prlogit "Pr(Prob) from Logit Model" . . est restore probitmod (results probitmod are active now) . predict prprobit (option pr assumed; Pr(vote_trump)) . lab var prprobit "Pr(Prob) from Probit Model" . . scatter prlogit prprobit, /// > title("[3.2.i] Comparison of Predicted Probs. from Logit and Probit") . . pwcorr prlogit prprobit | prlogit prprobit -------------+------------------ prlogit | 1.0000 prprobit | 0.9996 1.0000 ``` ![](fig/cda-03_02_i-trump-1.png){width=80% fig-alt="Scatterplot of predicted probabilities from the logit model against those from the probit model: the points fall almost exactly on a straight 45-degree line."} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} anes$prlogit <- predict(logitmod, newdata = anes, type = "response") anes$prprobit <- predict(probitmod, newdata = anes, type = "response") ggplot(anes, aes(x = prprobit, y = prlogit)) + geom_point() + labs(title = "[3.2.i] Comparison of Predicted Probs. from Logit and Probit", x = "Pr(Prob) from Probit Model", y = "Pr(Prob) from Logit Model") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](3-2-scaling-identification_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){fig-alt='Scatterplot of predicted probabilities from the logit model against those from the probit model: the points fall almost exactly on a straight 45-degree line.' width=80%} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} cor(anes$prlogit, anes$prprobit, use = "complete.obs") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` r-output [1] 0.9996027 ``` ::: ::: ::: ## Review of identification in BRM - The magnitude of the β's depends on the scale of the outcome - The size of the estimated β's ***cannot be directly interpreted*** as reflecting substantive effect size - ***The identifying assumption does not affect Pr(y=1\|x)*** - Probabilities, and marginal effects calculated from them, can be interpreted without concern about identification - This identification issue makes the coefficients have poor properties for determining: - Effect sizes - Group comparisons - Differences across nested models - E.g., Mediation - Interaction effects (AKA moderation)
